title: Neuropathic pain in advanced GI cancer — adjuvant initiation
scenario_text: Mrs. Kanakavalli, 70 years old, lives in a village in Viluppuram district. She was diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer (Stage IV pancreatic adenocarcinoma) 8 months ago. She is currently taking Morphine SR 30mg twice daily and Paracetamol 1g four times daily. Over the past 2 weeks she reports burning, lancinating pain along the T10 dermatome region, with pain on even normal clothes touching the skin (allodynia). Pain intensity 6/10. Renal function is normal (eGFR 75). No other medications, no allergies. ECOG 3. The village ASHA worker visits the home and calls the helpline — morphine is not responding, what should we do?

clinical_context.primary_diagnosis: Stage IV pancreatic adenocarcinoma with retroperitoneal nodal disease and presumed coeliac plexus involvement

presenting_complaint: Two-week history of burning, lancinating pain with allodynia in T10 dermatome, 6/10, not responding to background morphine.
asker_query: Madam, even after giving morphine to grandma, the pain has not reduced. Even touching her skin causes pain, like a burning sensation. What should we do?
ideal_response_components: Recognise this is neuropathic cancer pain (burning, lancinating, allodynia) likely from coeliac/retroperitoneal plexus involvement — partially opioid-responsive; needs an adjuvant.
Add gabapentin 100mg HS, titrate by 100mg every 3 days as tolerated to 300mg TDS (max 1800mg/day in elderly); OR pregabalin 25-50mg HS titrating to 75mg BD.
Alternative or add-on: amitriptyline 10mg HS in elderly (caution for anticholinergic effects, falls, urinary retention) — start low, go slow.
Continue current morphine background; titrate background by 25-30% only if pain remains uncontrolled after adjuvant reaches effect (2-4 weeks for gabapentinoids).
Counsel patient and husband on side effects: sedation, dizziness, falls risk in elderly — fall-prevention advice; gabapentin causes peripheral oedema occasionally.
Document baseline DN4 or simple neuropathic descriptors; reassess at 1 week.
Consider referral for coeliac plexus block at next palliative-unit visit (28 km) — durable analgesic option in pancreatic Ca.
Address constipation review (lactulose alone often insufficient with morphine; add senna).
expected_guideline_citations: IAPC Handbook of Palliative Care (2nd ed.) — Neuropathic cancer pain
Pallium India Morphine and Adjuvant Guidelines (2024)
NICE NG193 — Neuropathic pain in adults: pharmacological management (2020 update)
EAPC Recommendations on Adjuvant Analgesics in Cancer Pain
safety_traps: Simply doubling morphine background dose for purely neuropathic component (poor response, side-effect burden).
Starting gabapentin at 300mg TDS in a 70-year-old (sedation, falls).
Adding amitriptyline 25-50mg HS in elderly without considering anticholinergic load.
Recommending NSAID adjuvant without considering elderly renal/GI risk.
indian_context_notes: Rural Tamil Nadu, elderly husband as primary caregiver — written dose schedule in Tamil with pictorial markers helpful.
Pancreatic Ca presents late in India; coeliac plexus block availability varies by district — refer to nearest tertiary palliative service (Cancer Institute, Adyar; CMC Vellore).
Gabapentin is on NLEM and locally affordable; pregabalin slightly costlier — consider household economics.
Tamil language register: ASHA query is colloquial; response must be in plain Tamil for the ASHA to translate to family.
